text_blocks.snippet: Citizens and nationals of countries participating in the Visa Waiver Program (VWP) who plan to travel to the United States for tourism or business for 90 days or less are required to obtain authorization through the Electronic System for Travel Authorization (ESTA). This applies to travel by air, land, or sea. ESTA is an automated system that determines the eligibility of VWP travelers to enter the U.S., but it does not guarantee entry, which is determined by a Customs and Border Protection officer upon arrival.
snippet_highlighted_words: Citizens and nationals of countries participating in the Visa Waiver Program (VWP) who plan to travel to the United States for tourism or business for 90 days or less

list.title: Citizens/nationals of VWP countries:
list.snippet: If you are from a country that participates in the Visa Waiver Program and are traveling to the U.S. for tourism or business, you need ESTA.

list.title: Travelers staying 90 days or less:
list.snippet: ESTA is for stays of 90 days or less.

list.title: Travelers entering by air, sea, or land:
list.snippet: Regardless of the method of entry, if you are eligible for VWP, you need ESTA.

list.title: Even for transit through the U.S.:
list.snippet: If you are transiting the U.S. on your way to another country, and are from a VWP country, you need either ESTA or a visa.
Citizens of non-VWP countries: If your country is not part of the Visa Waiver Program, you will need a visa, not ESTA.
Travelers staying longer than 90 days: If you plan to stay longer than 90 days, you need a visa, not ESTA.
Those with a valid U.S. visa: If you already have a valid U.S. visa, you do not need ESTA.

Those who are not eligible for the VWP: Certain travelers, such as those who have been arrested, have a criminal record, or have been denied entry to the U.S. previously, may not be eligible for ESTA and may need a visa.

text_blocks.snippet: Citizens of countries not participating in the US Visa Waiver Program (VWP) require a visa to enter the United States. This includes countries not on the list of 40 VWP member countries. Additionally, certain individuals who are otherwise eligible for the VWP may be ineligible due to past travel to specific countries like Iran, Iraq, Syria, or due to dual nationality with one of those countries.

text_blocks.snippet: The U.S. Visa Waiver Program (VWP) allows citizens of certain countries to travel to the United States for tourism or business for up to 90 days without needing a visa. Currently, there are 40 countries participating in the VWP.
Here's a list of the countries whose citizens are eligible to participate in the Visa Waiver Program:

Andorra, Australia, Austria, Belgium, Brunei, Chile, Croatia, Czech Republic, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Iceland, Ireland, Israel, Italy, Japan, Latvia, Liechtenstein, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Malta, Monaco, Netherlands, New Zealand, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Qatar, San Marino, Singapore, Slovakia, Slovenia, South Korea, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, Taiwan, and United Kingdom.

list.title: ESTA:
list.snippet: Even with the VWP, travelers must obtain an Electronic System for Travel Authorization (ESTA) before traveling.

list.title: Duration of Stay:
list.snippet: The maximum stay allowed under the VWP is 90 days.

list.title: Exceptions:
list.snippet: There are exceptions to the VWP, including those who have traveled to certain countries, like Iran, Iraq, and Syria, on or after March 1, 2011.

list.title: Dual Nationals:
list.snippet: Dual nationals of VWP countries who are also nationals of Cuba, Iran, Iraq, North Korea, Sudan, or Syria may also be restricted.

list.title: Official Travel:
list.snippet: Limited exceptions exist for those traveling for diplomatic or military purposes in the service of a VWP country.
